raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

For the measured Kimi-K3 TP1/PP8 prefill workload, FlashInfer 0.7.1's 16K-token MoE candidate enumeration exposed token tiles 192 and 256. A supported tile128/config0 tactic, discovered through smaller-shape candidate enumeration and then executed at the real 16K shape, performed better on captured early/late-layer routing.

This ports the tile128 approach to the repository's pinned **FlashInfer 0.7.2**, using its existing cache-loading API. Re-enumeration on B30Z identified **tile128/config4**, and real captured-input replay verified that tactic and the new record. The older 0.7.1/config0 record is not installed or accepted. Tactic IDs are version-specific; no dependency downgrade or version-check bypass is included.

## Modifications

- Seed one serving-derived 16K MoE tuning bucket during startup, before the user's persistent cache is loaded. Explicit user-cache entries retain precedence; disabling cache reuse keeps fresh tuning behavior.
- Restrict loading to Kimi-K3, TP1/PP8/EP1, chunk16K, BF16 model dtype, SM103 and FlashInfer 0.7.2. FlashInfer's full environment metadata check further restricts the bundled record to the measured B30Z/CUDA/library combination.
- The cache key includes both activation/weight formats, local/global expert counts, top-k, hidden/intermediate dimensions, activation and weight layout, plus the unpacked routing representation.
- Fix the existing target/draft CUDA cache-phase fixture to supply the runner field read by the startup guard.
- Use the existing `load_configs` mechanism; do not replace `AutoTuner.choose_one`, add a process-wide monkey patch, or add a new configuration switch.

The record follows FlashInfer's tuning-bucket semantics. It is not a universal tile128 policy for arbitrary sequence lengths, models, hardware, EP or decode workloads. Existing explicit cache choices can override it.

## Accuracy Tests

- **2 unit tests passed**, with subcases rejecting other model types, parallelism, chunk sizes, dtypes, hardware and unvalidated FlashInfer 0.7.1/0.7.3.
- On B300/B30Z, loaded this branch's record with the real FlashInfer 0.7.2 `AutoTuner`, then replayed captured Kimi-K3 input `[16384, 3584]`, original expert weights, scales and top-k routing. The real operation selected **(128, 4)** and output was **bitwise equal** to the captured service reference.
- Loaded an explicit user record afterwards: the same real operation selected **(192, 4)**, confirming user-cache precedence; output again matched the reference bitwise.
- Ruff, isort, AST/JSON parsing, registered-test lint, and `git diff --check` passed.

The 0.7.2 Python wheel and its matching NVIDIA kernels were tested in an isolated overlay, retaining version checks; the installed 0.7.1 package was not modified. These verify the policy, public cache adapter and actual MoE operation.

Full-model serving validation now passes for these production changes on the common upstream `main` base `592754fc5e`, with FlashInfer 0.7.2; the standalone and repeated combined results are reported below. The current six full-service runs each pass 12 fixed greedy output checks covering input lengths 1,024 / 16,383 / 16,384 / 16,385 / 32,768 / 65,536, each repeated twice. All 60 comparisons against A1 match output token IDs and input SHA256 hashes. An additional eight C4 concurrent fixed-input checks match between A2 and B2. These are finite output-regression checks, not logits-level equality or a full task-accuracy benchmark.

### Cache-phase fixture review follow-up (2026-11-01)

Commit `cc5c303a8ec5db2c0168414c00f0a3b058161775` repairs the existing CUDA test fixture: initialize `is_draft_worker=False` for the target phase and set it to `True` before draft-cache loading. This commit changes only the test; the production code measured below is unchanged.

On B300/B30Z (SM103), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 and FlashInfer 0.7.2:

- The original `TestAutotuneCachePhases` reproduces `AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'is_draft_worker'`.
- After the fix, the complete `test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_flashinfer_autotune_sync.py`: **12 tests passed, 0 skipped**, including the real CUDA cache-phase case.
- `test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_kimi_k3_prefill_tactics.py`: **2 tests passed, 0 skipped**.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Full serving validation of the upstream integration (2026-11-01)

Tested production changes from #47651 (`7933473906e`) and #47653 (`34238f31a5d`) on the same upstream `main` base `592754fc5e`, using FlashInfer 0.7.2 for every arm. Kimi-K3, one 8-GPU B300/B30Z, TP1/PP8/EP1, chunk 16,384, pipeline async depth 1, client C4, ISL 65,536 / OSL 1. CUDA Graphs and radix caching disabled; model precision and all serving settings held fixed. Each formal run contains 128 requests after a separate 8-request warmup. Formal measurements exclude profiler/diagnostic requests and prototype hooks.

Each run uses an independent autotune cache cloned from the same baseline startup cache. Baseline/KDA caches contain no 16K MoE seed; MoE/combined caches contain the FlashInfer 0.7.2 `(128, 4)` record on all eight PP ranks. Separate post-benchmark Torch GPU traces of all eight PP ranks confirm the actual production paths: 1,104 KDA input-copy kernels become 276 pack kernels, and all 736 MoE GEMMs change token tile 192 to 128. These C1 diagnostic traces verify execution paths; their timings are not used as C4 serving measurements.

| Run | Requests | Input tok/s | P50 TTFT s | P99 TTFT s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline A1 | 128 | 42,203.78 | 6.128 | 7.046 |
| KDA only | 128 | 42,899.91 | 6.022 | 6.937 |
| MoE only | 128 | 42,813.05 | 6.034 | 6.926 |
| combined B1 | 128 | 43,569.94 | 5.925 | 6.835 |
| baseline A2 | 128 | 42,130.58 | 6.137 | 7.050 |
| combined B2 | 128 | 43,524.13 | 5.940 | 6.823 |
| baseline pooled | 256 | 42,167.15 | 6.132 | 7.359 |
| combined pooled | 256 | 43,547.02 | 5.930 | 7.125 |

MoE-only throughput changes by +1.44% against A1. This is one standalone screening pair. The repeated combined KDA+MoE result changes throughput by +3.27% (paired runs +3.24% / +3.31%); it must not be attributed to either PR alone. Pooled throughput is total input tokens / total formal duration; P50/P99 are recomputed from all formal request TTFTs. All 768 formal requests succeed with zero cached tokens and retractions. The combined pooled P50/P99 TTFT decrease by 3.28% / 3.17%; no formal request reaches 15 seconds. OSL is 1, so TPOT/ITL are not reported.

### Earlier prototype evidence

**Historical FlashInfer 0.7.1/config0 prototype measurements, not end-to-end measurements of the new 0.7.2/config4 startup-cache integration.** Kimi-K3 / SGLang 0.5.22 / FlashInfer 0.7.1, 8x B300, TP1/PP8, ISL 65,536 / OSL 1, chunk16K, client C4, unchanged precision, no profiler attached to formal requests.

| Configuration | Requests | Input tok/s | P50 TTFT s | P99 TTFT s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| same-condition baseline | 128 | 41,910.90 | 6.164 | 7.128 |
| MoE tile128/config0 only | 128 | 42,500.14 | 6.080 | 7.015 |

This single historical screening pair shows approximately **+1.41%** serving throughput; that historical pair is not a measurement of the 0.7.2 record and is not a repeated standalone result. The independently repeated **combined** MoE+KDA prototype achieved +3.12%/+3.32% and +3.14% in a longer 512-request-per-arm comparison. Those combined gains must not be attributed to this PR alone.

In matched-layer NSYS analysis of the combined prototype, MoE GEMM1+GEMM2 changed from 10.330 to 9.622 ms per invocation (about -6.85%). Smaller token tiles reduce estimated per-expert padding, but also change CTA counts and pipeline/resource use. Padding estimates and isolated NCU timing are not substitutes for serving measurements.

## Checklist

- [x] Preserve routing, weights, precision, dimensions and operation implementation.
- [x] Avoid process-wide method replacement and new environment switches.
- [x] Verify the real cached tactic, captured-tensor output and user-cache precedence.
- [x] Keep strict library/device metadata instead of assuming cross-version tactic compatibility.
- [x] Validate and add a new record for the pinned FlashInfer 0.7.2; reject other versions.
- [x] Complete common-base full-model serving validation, including repeated baseline/combined A/B and fixed output checks.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,31 @@
+"""Versioned serving-derived FlashInfer tactics for Kimi-K3 prefill."""
+
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+
+
+def load_kimi_k3_prefill_tactics(
+    tuner, *, model_type, tp_size, pp_size, ep_size, chunk_size, dtype, device
+):
+    """Seed the measured 16K bucket before loading the user's autotune cache.
+
+    This is a startup default, not a process-wide AutoTuner monkey patch.
+    FlashInfer's cache key includes the activation/weight formats, expert
+    geometry and routing representation. Its metadata check additionally
+    rejects other library builds and devices. Explicit user caches loaded
+    afterwards retain precedence. Do not reuse tactic IDs across versions.
+    """
+    import flashinfer
+
+    if (
+        model_type != "kimi_k3"
+        or (tp_size, pp_size, ep_size) != (1, 8, 1)
+        or chunk_size != 16384
+        or dtype != torch.bfloat16
+        or flashinfer.__version__ != "0.7.2"
+        or torch.cuda.get_device_capability(device) != (10, 3)
+    ):
+        return False
+    path = Path(__file__).with_name("configs") / "kimi_k3_sm103_fi072_prefill.json"
+    return tuner.load_configs(str(path))

@@ -328,6 +328,28 @@ def flashinfer_autotune_context(model_runner: ModelRunner, *, run_lm_head: bool)
         # autotune(cache=...) clears all file-loaded tactics on entry, which would drop
         # the target's tactics when the draft worker loads; load and save them by hand.
         tuner = AutoTuner.get()
+        if (
+            reuse_cache
+            and not mr.is_draft_worker
+            and get_exec().moe.moe_runner_backend == "flashinfer_mxfp4"
+            and "flashinfer::trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe" not in skip_ops
+        ):
+            from sglang.srt.layers.moe.flashinfer_kimi_k3_tactics import (
+                load_kimi_k3_prefill_tactics,
+            )
+
+            # Load serving-derived defaults first: an explicit user cache below
+            # must retain precedence, including a differently tuned 16K bucket.
+            load_kimi_k3_prefill_tactics(
+                tuner,
+                model_type=mr.model_config.hf_config.model_type,
+                tp_size=get_parallel().tp_size,
+                pp_size=get_parallel().pp_size,
+                ep_size=get_parallel().moe_ep_size,
+                chunk_size=max_prefill_buffer_tokens(),
+                dtype=mr.dtype,
+                device=mr.device,
+            )
         if reuse_cache and autotune_cache.is_file():
             tuner.load_configs(str(autotune_cache))
         mega_context = empty_context()

@@ -0,0 +1,85 @@
+import ast
+import json
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import Mock, patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.moe.flashinfer_kimi_k3_tactics import (
+    load_kimi_k3_prefill_tactics,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestKimiK3PrefillTactics(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.kwargs = dict(
+            model_type="kimi_k3",
+            tp_size=1,
+            pp_size=8,
+            ep_size=1,
+            chunk_size=16384,
+            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            device="cuda",
+        )
+
+    def test_only_the_validated_environment_is_seeded(self):
+        tuner = Mock()
+        tuner.load_configs.return_value = True
+        with (
+            patch.dict(
+                "sys.modules", {"flashinfer": SimpleNamespace(__version__="0.7.2")}
+            ),
+            patch("torch.cuda.get_device_capability", return_value=(10, 3)),
+        ):
+            self.assertTrue(load_kimi_k3_prefill_tactics(tuner, **self.kwargs))
+            path = Path(tuner.load_configs.call_args.args[0])
+            records = json.loads(path.read_text())
+            self.assertEqual(records.pop("_metadata")["flashinfer_version"], "0.7.2")
+            self.assertEqual(len(records), 1)
+            key, record = next(iter(records.items()))
+            op, runner, shapes, extras = ast.literal_eval(key)
